attempted_claim: Consider the focusing energy-critical NLS on R x R^d, d>=5: i u_t + Delta u + |u|^{4/(d-2)} u = 0, u(0)=u0 in Hdot^1(R^d), with E(u)=1/2||grad u||_2^2-(d-2)/(2d)||u||_{2d/(d-2)}^{2d/(d-2)} and S-norm ||u||_{L^{2(d+2)/(d-2)}(I x R^d)}. Let W be the ground state and W^+ the radial heteroclinic with E(W^+)=E(W), ||grad W^+||_2>||grad W||_2, T_+(W^+)=+inf, T_-(W^+)<inf. Let u be the maximal Hdot^1 solution on I with u0 in Hdot^1 cap L^2, E(u0)=E(W) and ||grad u0||_2>||grad W||_2 (kinetic-supercritical threshold, no symmetry assumption). Prove via concentration-compactness and profile decomposition that either (a) finite-lifespan S-blowup: |I|<inf with a finite endpoint T_pm<inf and ||u||_{S(0,T_pm)}=inf, or (b) u=W^+ modulo symmetries (phase, scaling, spatial translation, time translation and time reversal/conjugation), with (a) and (b) mutually exclusive and finite-time kept distinct from infinite-time S-blowup.
decisive_failure: The reported blockade is session-relative: it shows the full nonradial two-sided dichotomy could not be closed with bounded routine means, not that the target claim is false. Only elementary scaling and virial identities plus a drift-obstruction scaling model were verified computationally; no profile decomposition, rigidity theorem, or W^+ uniqueness result was proved. Literature search allowance was not consumed.
